extra.reason:
Registry rewritten as root -> {:delay :failures :created-at}.

- start! validates the banner: a non-map/EOF banner kills the child and throws with the exact `dart run` command to try by hand.
- The spawn lives inside a per-root delay, so swap! retries cannot duplicate it; concurrent first use shares one `dart run` (test asserts 8 threads -> 1 spawn).
- The displaced analyzer is stop!ed by whichever thread won the CAS that replaced it, and stop! now closes stdout as well as stdin before destroy-tree.
- Backoff 0/1s/2s/4s...60s per root, keyed off consecutive bad starts. A helper that served >=30s before dying is not counted as a failure, so an ordinary kill gets an immediate restart; a start that throws or a helper that dies young does.
- for-root throws instead of returning a broken record; daemon.clj turns that into a JSON-RPC error and extension.js already logs it.

New test/registry_test.clj (bb task test:registry, no Dart needed) stubs start!/alive?/stop! and covers reuse, single-flight, reaping, both backoff paths, window expiry, and shutdown/cache upkeep over a failed entry. Verified live too: with a bogus CLJD_RESOLVE_HELPER, 3 requests cost 2 dart invocations. test:parse, test:registry, test:extension, test:analyzer, test:resolve all green.

Closed ahead of its cljd-resolve-1sf.1 dependency (--force): the fixture/CI work is still open, but test:registry needs no Dart and no fixture and gives this change its own regression net.

Follow-up filed as cljd-resolve-1sf.12 (the banner read itself still has no deadline).

Integration suites now run against a target (test/cljd_resolve/test_target.clj): the checked-in Dart fixture in test/fixture by default, a real Flutter project via CLJD_TEST_PROJECT/CLJD_TEST_TARGET. No absolute paths left; dart pub get is self-healing; missing SDK is a SKIP unless CLJD_TEST_STRICT=1. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs core+fixture tiers on every push, flutter tier weekly/on-demand.

Request deadline around ask! (future + deref with timeout), generation-guarded eviction, and wedge-aware backoff. Also fixed kill!: it closed the streams before destroying the child, which deadlocks -- PushbackReader.read holds the reader's monitor and .close wants it, so the recovery path itself hung. Destroy now comes first. Covered by 12 new checks in test/registry_test.clj, each mutation-tested.

Client-side chunking. daemon.clj: warmUp now only starts the analyzer (an/for-file) and returns the lib list as :libs; new warmUpLib method warms one library and reports {:ok :lib :found}. extension.js: warmUp awaits the start request, then one warmUpLib per library, so a hover mid warm-up queues behind one chunk (~3s start, ~5.5s first SDK lib, ~10ms after) instead of the ~8s batch. Zero added concurrency in the daemon. Warm-up requests now honour the trace setting. Covered in test/extension_test.js (1 warmUp + 1 warmUpLib per library, off the trace log) and smoke-tested end to end against test/fixture with a real analyzer.

In-flight resolves are shared on {file,text,line,character} (extension.js resolveOnce + inFlight Map). The shared request carries NO token and is never cancelled; each consumer races it against its own token via raceCancellation, and the map entry is dropped in a .finally. README's 'a single resolve call' sentence corrected to 'one shared resolve call'. Three new checks in test/extension_test.js: one shared resolve for hover+definition on one cursor, consumer A cancels and B still gets the value, and a settled share is dropped rather than reused. All three mutation-tested (dropping the dedupe, putting the token on the shared request, and removing the finally each fail exactly one check).

line-index-cache is keyed on the path alone, with [stamp idx] as the value ([lastModified length] as the stamp), so a re-saved file replaces its entry instead of appending a permanent unreachable one. Verified directly: five saves of the same file leave one entry and the index is refreshed each time.

Direction B: the extension is installed from this checkout and there is no .vsix. The daemon cannot travel inside a package -- bin/cljd-resolve is babashka reading bb.edn and src/ at the repo root, driving a helper that needs a machine-local dart pub get in helper/ -- so the dead <extensionPath>/bin candidate is gone from daemonPath, the symlink install is documented as the supported one (README, *Installing it*), and extension/package.json declares "os": ["darwin", "linux"] plus "private": true. Windows follow-up filed as cljd-resolve-k7a.
README now describes the chunked warm-up: the Protocol method list carries warmUpLib alongside warmUp, and the Warm-up section explains why it is one request per library rather than one batch.

All 12 children complete. Verified: bb test green across six suites (340 checks, no skips, Dart fixture tier ran), bb test:vendor passes, vendored patch still confined to the one-line :required uncomment.
Added and exercised the Windows .cmd launcher, platform-specific selection and shell spawning, Windows PATH fallbacks, manifest support, tests, and documentation.
Classify helper local libraries against the explicit project root, with cwd-independent regression coverage
Added a one-shot target-library probe; unavailable libraries now use the existing SKIP/strict FAIL path. Full test suite and material_ui regression checks pass.
